source.title: The Entanglement Wall: Activation-Space Probes as Risk Detectors, Not Context Adjudicators

page_placements.theme: Projection onto the refusal direction as a readout and monitor: tracks the model's own refusal decision, works in distribution, fails under shift

record.tranche_reason: Uses a source-trained harmful-minus-harmless activation direction as a risk readout, but evaluates harmfulness classification and contextual transfer rather than refusal behavior or causal refusal mediation.
record.gate_note: The study fits and evaluates difference-in-means activation readouts, but does not measure refusal rates, ablate or add a refusal direction, or test the claim's other named mechanisms. Its results concern harmful-versus-harmless request classification and are recorded under fits_no_version. Related refusal-geometry results in the text are cited from other work and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction only as a scalar harmfulness-risk readout. It evaluates AUROC, pair ranking and threshold errors on matched requests. It never measures refusal rates, never ablates or adds the direction, and never tests jailbreaks, geometry, transfer of a refusal direction, or reasoning models. Its results do not bear on whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Strong broad-source ranking did not give reliable operating decisions on matched same-topic pairs: source thresholds blocked most legitimate requests, and recalibration left substantial error. Three readouts met the Wall criteria and two were mixed. Matched-label training recovers the distinction, and lexical controls show similar transfer loss. The claims are limited to the evaluated configurations.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a source-fit harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction, but as a scalar harmfulness-risk readout rather than a refusal intervention. The study uses raw AdvBench and Alpaca prompts, maximum pooling, and post-attention layer-normalization activations; it does not project the direction out or add it to activations.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different outcomes across checkpoints and readout constructions. Its primary readout uses selected layers and componentwise maximum pooling; alternative source-trained classifiers change the detection/false-blocking profile. The surface-form analysis also reports pooling-dependent degradation. These are sensitivities of its harmfulness-detection analyses, not tests of refusal mediation.

fits_no_version.finding: Source-trained harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference readouts reach 0.996–0.999 broad AUROC but 0.701–0.860 on matched same-topic pairs. Pair ranking stays at 0.829–0.929, central score intervals overlap, and CV-BTE after recalibration is 0.229–0.329.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A broad-source harmfulness direction preserves within-pair ordering but transfers poorly as an absolute decision boundary to legitimate same-topic requests.

fits_no_version.finding: At unchanged source thresholds, Twin-70 TPR is 0.943–1.000, while the false-block rate on harmless matched requests is 0.686–0.986. XSTest false blocking is only 0.000–0.012.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A source-derived harmfulness threshold detects harmful same-topic requests while blocking most legitimate matched requests.

fits_no_version.finding: In two abliterated (refusal-modified) checkpoints, a harmful-minus-harmless prompt direction still separates broad harmful from harmless requests at AUROC 0.998–0.999. The authors do not isolate the effect of refusal modification.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmfulness information remains linearly readable in prompt activations after refusal abliteration.

record.problems: The matched cohorts are synthetic and English-only, and authorization or real-world context is not independently verified. The authors report no independent human re-annotation of the cohorts. They note that several other readout and training settings remain untested, and that the tested thresholds and finite cohorts do not estimate deployment rates. The study does not assess general capability or refusal behavior.
record.rows_left_out: No results bearing directly on the listed refusal-claim versions were available to extract. Adjacent results not itemized include secondary-cohort operating points and transfer AUROC, alternative source-trained logistic/RBF/MLP readouts, lexical controls, matched-label classifiers, reference-fitted readouts, generation-time sensors, and the surface-form diagnostic; these concern harmfulness detection/readout behavior rather than refusal-direction mediation.

untested.parts: No refusal measured; no ablation or addition of the direction; no capability check.
Uses two publicly abliterated checkpoints but does not measure their refusal or perform any weight edit.
No jailbreak or adversarial-training test. The surface-form transformations measure readout threshold crossings, not attack success.
No test of refusal geometry as affine, conic or multi-directional.
Harmfulness readouts are not compared against refusal behavior. The refusal-modified versus unmodified comparison is explicitly not isolated.
Readouts are fitted per checkpoint; there is no cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer of a refusal direction.

record.verdict_notes: Arditi et al. is cited only in related work on refusal geometry. The readout adapts Llorente-Saguer's harmful-intent direction (AdvBench minus Alpaca, max pooling, post-attention layernorm), not the refusal direction as an intervention. The reader's T4/uses_without_test is acceptable; T6 would also be defensible. No verdict labels are given because no version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: No refusal behavior is measured; no direction is ablated or added; no general-capability check is reported.
No weight edit or released-model refusal removal is tested.
No jailbreak is tested as suppressing a refusal direction, and no training against such ablation is performed.
No refusal-direction geometry is tested as affine, conic, or multi-directional.
The study does not test whether harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are encoded separately.
Readouts are fitted separately per checkpoint; there is no cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test of a refusal direction.
The study compares checkpoints but does not manipulate refusal-training method or timing to test direction formation.
No reasoning model or reason-before-answer condition is evaluated.

relation.reason: Arditi et al. is cited only in Related Work. The mean-difference direction and the abliterated models are used without testing whether the direction mediates refusal. The text says effects of refusal modification are not isolated (Section III-B).

tranche.reason: The study uses a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, the refusal-direction construction, only as a scalar harmfulness readout (AUROC, pair ranking, CV-BTE, threshold errors). It also uses two abliterated checkpoints as subjects. It never measures refusal rates and never ablates or adds the direction. It reports only its own readout's performance.

source_check.notes: The Llama 3.1 8B and Qwen 2.5 7B subjects are abliterated community checkpoints (mlabonne/..., huihui-ai/...; Appendix E-A), so the subject fields for R1, R3, R6, R8, R11, R13, R26 and R28 need fixing. The readout differs from Arditi's extraction: max-pooled over the first 64 prompt tokens, post-attention layer-norm output, no chat template. It is a harmfulness probe, not a refusal test, so verdicts of none for all versions are right.

statements.problem: Numbers match the abstract, Section IV-A and Table III, all for Twin-70. The statement does not say that two of the five checkpoints (Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B) are abliterated variants. That is an omission, not an error.
